newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai animal feed industry to boycott EU materials.
newsitem.headline: Thai animal feed industry to boycott EU materials.

text.p: Thai Feedmill Association will boycott feed raw materials from the European Union to retaliate against the group's elimination of trade privileges on Thai shrimp, the head of the association said on Monday.

Prasit Damrongchietanon, Thai Feedmill Association president, told Reuters that his group will immediately begin the boycott on 2.0 billion baht ($76.9 million) a year of feed raw materials from the EU. The raw materials include vitamins, minerals and fishmeal.
"We will turn to Asian markets such as Japan or South Korea or the United States for the materials instead," he said.
Prasit said the decision was made after a meeting on Monday with groups of shrimp farmers and frozen shrimp exporters who were hit by the EU's move.
The EU in January cut trade privileges under the Generalised System of Preferences for Thai shrimp exports by half, making Thailand less competitive in that market.

"If they (shrimp farmers, exporters) are affected, we will be too because they buy shrimp feed from us. So, we will accept their request that any feed raw materials from EU be boycotted," Prasit told Reuters.
"We think the trade privilege was removed unfairly," he added.
Thailand in 1996 exported 161,486 tonnes of shrimps worth 43.4 billion baht. The exports to the EU amounted to 19,237 tonnes and fetched 4.5 billion baht in foreign exchange.
Although Thai shrimp exports to the EU are relatively small compared to those to the United States and Japan, its demand has potential to grow, Prasit said.
Thai shrimp exports to the United States and Japan combined in 1996 totalled 106,101 tonnes, according to official figures. ($1 = 26 baht)
